sn11.6:1.2: “Bhikkhus, once in the past the devas and the asuras were arrayed for battle.
sn11.6:1.3: In that battle the asuras won and the devas were defeated.
sn11.6:1.4: In defeat the devas withdrew towards the north while the asuras pursued them.
sn11.6:1.5: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Matali in verse:
sn11.6:2.1: “‘Avoid, O Matali, with your chariot pole
sn11.6:2.2: The bird nests in the silk-cotton woods;
sn11.6:2.3: Let’s surrender our lives to the asuras
sn11.6:2.4: Rather than make these birds nestless.’
sn11.6:3.1: “‘Yes, your lordship,’ Matali the charioteer replied, and he turned back the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds.
sn11.6:3.2: “Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to the asuras:
sn11.6:3.3: ‘Now Sakka’s chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds has turned back.
sn11.6:3.4: The devas will engage in battle with the asuras for a second time.’ Stricken by fear, they entered the city of the asuras.
sn11.6:3.5: In this way, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, won a victory by means of righteousness itself.”
